rows.title: CT is much stronger fiscally as it tip-toes over spending cap
rows.standfirst: To bolster local schools, Gov. Ned Lamont and the General Assembly will exceed CT’s spending cap in a fashion not seen in nearly two decades.

rows.title: CT legislature adopts $28B budget with big aid for towns, childcare
rows.standfirst: The CT legislature adopted a $28.1 billion budget Saturday that orders big new investments in municipal aid and affordable childcare.

rows.title: Advocates press Lamont to aid thousands losing food benefits
rows.standfirst: Anti-hunger advocates are focused on Gov. Ned Lamont in their push to intensify aid for residents who have lost federal nutrition benefits.

rows.title: CT Senate pulls all-nighter, rearranging budget and passing gun bill
rows.standfirst: The Senate stayed overnight to pass a gun control bill and legislation that makes millions in revisions to the state’s already-adopted budget.

rows.title: Lawmakers solve town aid riddle on third try
rows.standfirst: The General Assembly OK’d a bill clarifying that towns could reopen their budgets to use increased state aid to reduce local property taxes.

rows.title: New CT budget sets Lamont’s legacy as he seeks 3rd term
rows.standfirst: As he runs for a third term, a piece of Gov. Ned Lamont’s legacy already is established: He’s reduced CT’s debt at unmatched speed and scale.

rows.title: Lamont noncommittal on federal scholarship tax credit after NY moves to join
rows.standfirst: Under the program, donors to scholarship granting organizations receive the full donation amount back—up to $1700—as a federal tax credit.

rows.title: Surging gas prices shine spotlight on CT’s fuel taxes
rows.standfirst: A tax cap has been mitigating pain at the pumps since March, but recent price hikes have some ready to revisit Connecticut’s fuel tax system.

rows.title: Higher gas prices could strain CT’s transportation rebuild plans
rows.standfirst: Certain gasoline and sales tax receipts could “soften” this summer if prices remain elevated or turn worse in the coming months.
